To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neural marker of error detection, the Pe, is graded by confidence in correct decisions.

The neural marker of error detection (i.e. the error positivity) is graded with subjective confidence in correct trials and that this relationship is independent of objective accuracy, and that neural markers of confidence in correct choices are predictive of error detection in incorrect choices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people know that their thoughts and actions are correct.
the mechanisms underlying metacognitive judgments, which are essential for the self-monitoring of thoughts, feelings, and actions.
understanding how the brain makes judgments about its own judgments and actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
confidence is a graded, subjective evaluation of the quality of the decision process and that error detection is an objective, conscious awareness of an incorrect decision.
the Pe is not just a marker of awareness of errors, but rather a graded marker of the confidence in decisions, both correct and incorrect, that is, the degree of subjective certainty in the decision.
confidence and error detection share neural markers in human decision-making.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pe is not only an error signal but also a confidence signal.
the neural markers of confidence and error are highly related and can be explained by the same underlying neural mechanisms.
the neural markers of decision confidence and error detection are overlapping, but not identical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural mechanisms of confidence and error detection are closely linked, with the former being predictive of the latter and both being predictive of the accuracy of the preceding choice.
the error positivity (a neural index of error awareness) is not just an index of error detection, but also an index of confidence.
confidence and error detection are not independent processes.
